This was a catastrophic year: the auditor (Khan Wahab Shafique Rahman & Co.) issued a Qualified Opinion with a 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' paragraph, citing Solo CRAR of 4.92% (required 12.50%), an LCR of 22.75% (required >=100%), an NSFR of 71.80% (required >100%), and an Investment-Deposit Ratio of 122.25% (required <=92%). Percentage of Classified Investments against total Investments (Annexure-B) = 91.75% (BDT 559,203.17mn classified out of BDT 609,513.24mn total investment) -- up from 3.95% in FY2023, the sharpest single-year deterioration of any bank/year found in this dataset so far. Bangladesh Bank letter no. DBI-06/51(2)/2025-373 dated 27/04/2025 assessed a large deficit provision; per Note 8.9 of the financial statements, required provision against investments as per CL = BDT 494,979.21mn (49,497.92 crore) against provision maintained of BDT 16,361.94mn (1,636.19 crore) -- a shortfall of BDT 478,617.27mn (47,861.73 crore). Bangladesh Bank letter no. DOS(CAMS)1157/41(Dividend)/2025-3100 dated 21/05/2025 permitted the Bank to finalize these audited financial statements WITHOUT addressing this deficit provision (regulatory forbearance). NOTE: the Auditors' Report itself (Basis for Qualified Opinion, para 1) cites DIFFERENT figures for the SAME Bangladesh Bank letter (DBI-06/51(2)/2025-373 dated 27/04/2025): required provision BDT 50,994.06 crore, provision maintained BDT 1,895.34 crore, shortfall BDT 49,098.71 crore -- these are recorded verbatim here rather than reconciled with Note 8.9's figures, per project convention of never silently reconciling divergent source figures. The Auditors' going-concern paragraph separately estimates total investments at ~Tk 60,915 crore of which ~Tk 49,439 crore (~81%) are classified/impaired -- a third, independently-worded figure, again different from both Note 8.9's CL-schedule classified base (BDT 507,341.46mn = 83.24% of total investment) and Annexure-B's 'Amount of Classified Investments' (BDT 559,203.17mn = 91.75%). All three classified-investment figures coexist within the same audited financial statements; none is corrected or superseded by another as far as this document shows. The auditor also disclosed extensive fraud-pattern findings under 'Other Matters': irregular investment disbursements using borrower identities that may not reflect actual customers, ACC (Anti-Corruption Commission) legal proceedings and asset freezes against bank officials, a Bangladesh Bank forensic audit and special task force, overvalued collateral (esp. land), and investment disbursements exceeding sanctioned limits via unauthorized internal Commitment IDs. risk_signals.statement: This bank did not merely deteriorate in FY2024 -- it failed. Percentage of Classified Investments exploded from 3.95% (FY2023) to 91.75% (FY2024, BDT 559,203.17mn of BDT 609,513.24mn total investment). Solo CRAR collapsed to 4.92% against a 12.50% requirement, with a Capital Surplus/(deficit) against Minimum Capital Requirement of BDT -29,228.15mn (i.e. the bank needed BDT 57,589.40mn of regulatory capital and had BDT 28,361.26mn). The auditor (Khan Wahab Shafique Rahman & Co.) issued a Qualified Opinion plus a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph, and separately calculated that if the full assessed provisioning shortfall were recognized, CRAR would fall to approximately (80.00)% to (80.39)%. Per Note 8.9, required provision against investments was BDT 494,979.21mn against BDT 16,361.94mn maintained (deficit BDT 478,617.27mn = 47,861.73 crore) -- Bangladesh Bank explicitly permitted the bank to publish these audited financial statements without booking this deficit (letter DOS(CAMS)1157/41(Dividend)/2025-3100 dated 21/05/2025). FY2024 profit after tax was BDT -3,993.40mn (EPS -3.31) vs +3,240.09mn (EPS 2.82) in FY2023. Subsequent events (outside the FY2024 report but confirmed via DSE disclosures and independent web research): Bangladesh Bank declared the bank 'non-viable' and suspended trading effective 5 November 2025 under the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025; on 9 November 2025 Bangladesh Bank issued a Letter of Intent merging this bank with Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, and EXIM Bank (also in this dataset) into a new state-owned entity, 'Sammilito Islami Bank'; a Capital Reduction Order dated 21 December 2025 wrote the bank's entire paid-up capital (BDT 1,208.14 crore) down to ZERO and cancelled all shares, effective 5 November 2025; the bank was placed in DSE 'Z' category on 4 January 2026 for failing to hold its FY2024 AGM. No FY2025 annual report exists or is expected to -- see data_gaps. This is the most severe single-year/single-bank deterioration found anywhere in this 36-bank dataset to date, exceeding even NBL's FY2024 balance-sheet insolvency (equity -24,003mn, CAR -5.48%) and ISLAMIBANK's FY2024 under-provisioning (884,350mn unprovided = 12.7x equity) in that FIRSTSBANK's institutional existence itself did not survive past FY2024.

The FY2024 Auditors' Report's 'Other Matters' section documents, in the auditor's own words: (1) 'irregular investment disbursements... involving the use of borrower identities that may not have reflected actual customers' with 'a portion of the disbursed funds may have been misappropriated', Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) legal proceedings and asset freezes against bank officials, and a Bangladesh Bank forensic audit with a special task force and international auditors engaged to trace fund movements; (2) investment proceeds used to settle liabilities of 'other entities under common control' with 'patterns of inter-borrower fund transfers' disguised as unrelated transactions; (3) inadequately disclosed contingent liabilities tied to the classified-investment portfolio; (4) overvaluation of collateral (particularly land) 'exceeding actual purchase or mouza values'; (5) investment disbursements exceeding sanctioned limits via unauthorized internal 'Commitment IDs' issued by Head Office without formal amendments; and (6) undocumented placement agreements with Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC, Rupali Bank PLC, and Janata Bank PLC. Separately, the Emphasis of Matter section describes IT-control failures: 'The Bank's CIPPS was manipulated to enhance investment limits without proper approval.' This is direct auditor-sourced evidence (not third-party allegation) of the S. Alam Group-era related-party lending abuse flagged as a governance risk in this bank's FY2019 report (see the related_party_governance_signal below), now realized.

The FY2024 audited financial statements contain unreconciled internal inconsistencies, recorded here verbatim rather than reconciled, per project convention. (a) Note 8.9 and the Auditors' Report's 'Basis for Qualified Opinion' both cite the SAME Bangladesh Bank letter (DBI-06/51(2)/2025-373 dated 27/04/2025) but state different required-provision figures: BDT 49,497.92 crore (Note 8.9) vs BDT 50,994.06 crore (Auditors' Report), a BDT 1,496.34 crore difference. (b) Three different classified-investment figures coexist in the same document: 91.75% / BDT 559,203.17mn (Annexure-B, 'Amount of Classified Investments'); 83.24% / BDT 507,341.46mn (Note 8.9's CL-classification base: Sub-standard + Doubtful + Bad&Loss); and ~81% / ~BDT 494,390mn (the Auditors' Report's going-concern paragraph). None of the three is flagged in the source document as superseding another.

Investment-Deposit ratio jumped from 103.13% (FY2022) to 118.45% (FY2023) as total deposits fell (BDT 473,046mn -> BDT 455,195mn) while investments kept growing — a level well above the typical <100% norm seen in FY2011-2019 (peak 93.15% in FY2018) and a liquidity-strain signal. This continued into FY2024: IDR reached 122.25% even as total deposits fell further to BDT 431,431.01mn, and the Auditors' Report separately disclosed a Liquidity Coverage Ratio of just 22.75% (required >=100%) and a Net Stable Funding Ratio of 71.80% (required >100%) at FY2024 year-end.

Percentage of Classified Investments (this bank's NPL-equivalent) rose from 4.39% (FY2020) to a peak of 4.73% (FY2021), then improved to 3.95% (FY2023) — a milder and more contained pattern than the sharp FY2024 spikes seen at conventional banks in this dataset at the time. This proved to be the calm before the collapse: see regulatory_resolution_and_failure_fy2024_fy2025 above for the FY2024 explosion to 91.75%.

Newly-added Q1-Q3 un-audited interim filings (added 2026-08-27) show the FY2024 collapse was NOT a single hidden event -- it was a real, accelerating, quantifiable deterioration visible in the bank's own quarterly disclosures from Q2 2024 onward, culminating in a sudden catastrophic recognition specifically in Q4. Discrete-quarter Net Profit After Tax (Solo): Q1 2024 +BDT 361.03mn, Q2 2024 +BDT 528.20mn (still growing), Q3 2024 -BDT 274.93mn (the first quarterly LOSS, filed/signed 2024-10-31, versus +BDT 363.98mn in the same quarter of 2023) -- Total Operating Income (discrete) nearly halved year-over-year in Q3 alone (BDT 2,380.54mn vs BDT 3,628.80mn). Cumulative 9-month (Jan-Sep 2024) profit was still positive at +BDT 614.30mn. Subtracting this from the already-stored FY2024 full-year loss (BDT -3,993.40mn, from 2024_Q4.json) implies a Q4-2024-alone (Oct-Dec) loss of approximately BDT -4,607.70mn -- 115% of the entire reported annual loss, meaning the full-year loss is smaller in magnitude than the implied Q4 loss alone because Q1-Q3 was net profitable. A leading indicator was visible even earlier and accelerating fast: cumulative 'Specific Provision for Classified Investment' (the only asset-quality-adjacent figure disclosed at interim frequency by this bank) went BDT +144.53mn (Q1) -> +593.78mn (H1, i.e. +449.25mn in Q2 alone, 3.1x Q1's charge) -> +1,800.39mn (9m, i.e. +1,206.61mn in Q3 alone, 2.7x Q2's charge) -- roughly tripling quarter-on-quarter, a full 7-8 months before the FY2024 audited financial statements (finalized ~2025-05-29) revealed Classified Investments had reached 91.75% and Solo CRAR had collapsed to 4.92%. CRITICALLY, no Classified-Investment percentage or CRAR figure is disclosed in ANY of this bank's un-audited interim (Q1/H1/Q3) filings at any point in 2024 or any other year -- these headline crisis metrics only ever surfaced in the year-end audited statements, meaning a market participant reading only the interim filings would have seen mounting stress (accelerating provisions, a swing to a quarterly loss) but had no way to see the true 91.75%/4.92% scale until the audit. The crisis did not stop at FY2024 year-end: subsequently-filed un-audited Q1 2025 (signed 2025-05-29, the same day the audited FY2024 statements were adopted) and Q2 2025 (signed 2025-07-30) filings show losses of BDT -5,755.73mn and BDT -11,170.09mn respectively -- each individually larger than the entire FY2024 annual loss -- driven in Q1 2025 by Net Investment Income itself turning negative (Profit Paid on Deposits of BDT 10,424.43mn EXCEEDING Investments Income of BDT 6,852.81mn), eroding Solo Total Shareholders' Equity from BDT 20,069.13mn (31-Dec-2024) to just BDT 3,143.31mn (30-Jun-2025) -- i.e. down to roughly 26% of paid-up capital alone -- months before Bangladesh Bank's Capital Reduction Order (effective 5-Nov-2025) formally wrote capital to zero.

Several directors profiled in the FY2019 annual report hold concurrent director/shareholder positions across numerous S. Alam Group-affiliated companies (S. Alam Cement, S. Alam Steels, S. Alam Vegetable Oil, S. Alam Power Plant, S. Alam Properties, and others). This is the same conglomerate whose related-party lending exposure is documented to have caused a severe FY2024 asset-quality and capital-adequacy shock at EXIM Bank (also in this dataset) following Bangladesh's 2024 political transition. This forecast is now confirmed and realized: see regulatory_resolution_and_failure_fy2024_fy2025 and auditor_fraud_findings_fy2024 above -- this bank was placed under Bangladesh Bank resolution in November 2025 and merged into a new state-owned bank alongside EXIM Bank and three other S. Alam-linked Islamic banks.

insights.historical_context: First Security Islami Bank ran a conventional, moderately-growing Islamic banking franchise from FY2011-2023 (assets BDT 91,013mn to BDT 659,114mn, classified investments consistently under 5%), with an emerging FY2023 liquidity-strain signal (deposits falling while investments grew) set against a governance backdrop of heavy S. Alam Group director overlap. FY2024 is where the S. Alam Group-linked related-party lending abuse, already documented as a severe FY2024 shock at EXIM Bank elsewhere in this dataset, hit this bank directly and catastrophically: classified investments exploded to 91.75% of the portfolio, Solo CRAR collapsed to 4.92% (vs 12.5% required, and as low as -80% on a fully-provisioned basis per the auditor), and the FY2024 Auditors' Report documents auditor-identified fraud patterns (fictitious borrower identities, inter-related-party fund transfers, ACC criminal proceedings, a Bangladesh Bank forensic audit). Unlike every other bank in this dataset, FIRSTSBANK's story does not continue into FY2025 as the same entity: Bangladesh Bank declared it non-viable in November 2025 and merged it, with zero residual share value, into a new state-owned bank ('Sammilito Islami Bank') together with Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, and EXIM Bank. This makes FIRSTSBANK's FY2024 figures a rare directly-observed 'end state' of the exact mechanism (S. Alam Group related-party lending) that this dataset's insights for EXIM Bank and other banks could previously only infer was in progress.

sources.reporting_basis: SOLO / STANDALONE. Determined 2026-08-26 by matching the total assets and total regulatory capital this dataset records against the balance sheets and Basel-III CRAR disclosures in the bank's own FY2024 audited financial statements (firstsbank-annual-report-2024.txt, printed pp.6 and 62-63). Evidence: FY2023 total assets of 659,114.06mn (already stored in 2023_Q4.json) match this report's Solo 'BALANCE SHEET' comparative column exactly (659,114,061,504); the Solo 'A. Total Regulatory Capital' comparative column for FY2023 (40,674,859,096) also matches this dataset's stored total_capital (40674.86mn) exactly. The Consolidated Balance Sheet and Consolidated CRAR disclosure in the same report show different FY2023 figures (Consolidated total assets/liabilities+equity approx. 660,110.64mn; Consolidated Total Regulatory Capital 40,896,434,594) -- confirming Solo and Consolidated are genuinely different bases here (the bank has two subsidiaries, First Security Islami Capital & Investment Ltd. and First Security Islami Exchange Italy S.R.L.) and that every year in this dataset (which has always cited '(Solo)'-labelled tables) is on the Solo basis.
sources.notes: annual_reports/FIRSTSBANK archive covers 2011-2024 (14 years). FY2025 confirmed unavailable and very likely permanently so -- see the 2024-2025 source entry below. Shariah-based Islamic bank; reports 'Investment' rather than conventional 'Loans and Advances', and 'Classified Investments' rather than 'NPL'. The 2019 and 2021 reports' multi-year summary tables are presented as scanned/image-based pages in the source PDFs (pdftotext extracted only garbled or empty text for these specific pages, despite the rest of each document extracting normally); those two tables were re-extracted via direct vision reading of the rendered PDF page images, cross-validated against the balance sheet identity. sources.notes: No FY2025 annual report, audited financial statements, or 'Yearly Statement' PDF exists for First Security Islami Bank PLC as a standalone entity, and this is very likely a permanent series-end rather than a routine lag. Evidence chain, all independently verified: (1) fsibplc.com has no 'Yearly_statement2025.pdf'/'Annual-Report-2025.pdf' under any filename variant tried (confirmed 404 live); (2) DSE's price-sensitive-news archive for FIRSTSBANK (dsebd.org/old_news.php?inst=FIRSTSBANK) shows its auditor gave a Qualified Opinion with a Material-Uncertainty-Related-to-Going-Concern paragraph for FY2024 (disclosed 2025-06-19), the FY2024 AGM (originally scheduled 2025-09-15) was postponed indefinitely (disclosed 2025-08-25), Bangladesh Bank declared the bank 'non-viable' and suspended trading effective 5 November 2025 under the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025 (disclosed 2025-11-06), a Capital Reduction Order dated 21 December 2025 wrote the bank's entire paid-up capital (BDT 1,208.14 crore) down to ZERO and cancelled all shares effective 5 November 2025 (disclosed 2025-12-24), and the bank was placed in 'Z' category on 4 January 2026 for failing to hold its AGM (the most recent disclosure found; nothing newer as of retrieval); (3) independent web search confirms Bangladesh Bank issued a Letter of Intent on 9 November 2025 for a new state-owned bank, 'Sammilito Islami Bank', merging First Security Islami Bank PLC together with Global Islami Bank PLC, Social Islami Bank PLC, Union Bank PLC, and Export Import Bank of Bangladesh PLC (EXIMBANK -- also in this dataset, confirmed independently by the agent working that bank) under the S. Alam Group-linked resolution program, with all five banks' shares written down to zero. Because the resolution/merger process was already underway before FY2025 (Jan-Dec 2025) even closed, and the bank's normal AGM/audit cycle was disrupted and then superseded by the merger, there is no realistic expectation that a standalone FY2025 'First Security Islami Bank PLC' annual report will ever be filed; any FY2025-and-later reporting for this banking business will presumably surface (if at all) under 'Sammilito Islami Bank' rather than 'FIRSTSBANK'. The latest actual financial data point found for this entity is a revised, unaudited, 9-month Q3 2025 (Jan-Sep 2025) interim statement (DSE disclosure 2025-12-14/2025-12-27) showing Consolidated NAV per share of Tk (460.18) as at 30 September 2025 after Bangladesh Bank cancelled an earlier deferral facility and forced full provisioning -- this is a partial-year, unaudited, deeply-negative-equity data point and per this project's 'quarterly only, never backfill/fabricate a year-end from a partial period' rule it was NOT used to construct a 2025_Q4.json. No 2025_Q4.json file was created for this bank.

sources.note: Found by browsing fsibplc.com's 'Statement' navigation link (statement.php 404s directly, but the underlying /File/statement/quarterly/ and /File/statement/half_yearly/ directory paths, discovered via Wayback CDX enumeration of fsibplc.com/File/statement/, are live and directly downloadable -- all files in this batch returned live HTTP 200, no Wayback needed). All files are clean, born-digital PDFs (not scanned/OCR-needed) with a highly consistent structure across all 5 years: CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED BALANCE SHEET, CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED PROFIT AND LOSS ACCOUNT, CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED CASH FLOW STATEMENT, CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED STATEMENT OF CHANGES IN EQUITY, then the same four statements again on a Solo (non-consolidated) basis, then shared notes (Solo notes suffixed '(a)'). Solo basis used throughout, consistent with every other year in this dataset. Every year's Half-Yearly (Jan-Jun) and Q3 (Jan-Sep) filing prints BOTH a cumulative-from-Jan-1 column AND a separate discrete-single-quarter column (e.g. 'Jan'24 to Sep'24' and 'Jul'24 to Sep'24' side by side) -- both were captured (suffixes '_cumulative' and '_discrete_q'), both basis='reported' since both are directly printed by the bank, not derived by subtraction. Q1 filings only ever have one column (cumulative=discrete for a first quarter). No CRAR/Capital-to-RWA ratio and no Classified-Investment amount/percentage is disclosed anywhere in these condensed interim filings at any point in the 2021-2025 span -- the only interim asset-quality-adjacent figure available is 'Specific Provision for Classified Investment' (a P&L note sub-line, cumulative from Jan 1), captured as 'specific_provision_classified_investment_cumulative'. Cross-validated exhaustively: every filing's own prior-year-end comparative Total Assets/Equity column matches this dataset's already-stored FY2020/2021/2022/2023/2024 Q4 total_assets and total_equity figures to the taka (after rounding) -- see each quarterly JSON's period_note -- confirming Solo-basis continuity and no restatement across this entire span. See insights.json for the major finding this unlocked: a real-time-visible, accelerating deterioration through 2024 (profit swinging to a discrete Q3 2024 loss; Specific Provision for Classified Investment roughly tripling quarter-on-quarter) well before the FY2024 audited collapse, with an implied Q4-2024-alone loss (calculated by subtracting this batch's own Q3 2024 9-month cumulative profit from the already-stored FY2024 annual profit) of approximately BDT -4,608mn -- larger than the entire reported annual loss. Board-meeting dates (Q1 2025 and Half-Yearly 2025 adopted 2025-05-29 and 2025-07-30 respectively) confirm the crisis continued deepening well past FY2024 year-end: Q1 2025 alone lost BDT -5,755.73mn and Q2 2025 alone lost BDT -11,170.09mn (both un-audited), eroding Solo equity from BDT 20,069.13mn (31-Dec-2024) to just BDT 3,143.31mn (30-Jun-2025) -- these two periods are OUTSIDE this dataset's core FY2011-2024 coverage but were included as valuable, genuinely-sourced post-collapse trajectory context per this task's request.

sources.note: Found via Wayback CDX enumeration of fsiblbd.com/wp-content/uploads/. Same Consolidated-then-Solo condensed-statement structure as the 2021+ batch, confirming this format predates the fsibplc.com site redesign; earliest labels use non-'/(Loss)' phrasing ('Profit before Provision and Tax', 'Net Profit after Tax'/'Net Profit after tax' -- inconsistent capitalisation between files) and, in the very oldest (Q1 2018), a single combined 'Provision for Taxation' line instead of a Current/Deferred split -- both handled with case-insensitive, alternate-label-matching extraction and cross-validated via the balance-sheet identity and full profit-chain arithmetic (income-expense=PBPT; PBPT-provisions=PBT; PBT-tax=PAT) on every single period, all of which reconcile exactly. IMPORTANT WAYBACK TRAP ENCOUNTERED REPEATEDLY IN THIS BATCH: several of these URLs have multiple archived captures where the largest CDX-declared 'length' actually downloads as a genuinely-truncated-at-the-source stub, confirmed via response headers ('x-archive-orig-content-length: 1048576' + 'warning: 299 wayback content truncated by "length"') and pdfinfo syntax errors -- i.e. the ORIGINAL crawl, not Wayback's replay, only fetched the first 1 MiB. This is the same trap already documented in this project's Wayback-truncation memory note, but this session found it applies even when the CDX API's own reported 'length' field for that specific capture is UNDER 1,048,576 bytes (misleadingly suggesting it's fine) -- the only reliable check is downloading and running pdfinfo, not trusting CDX metadata alone. Resolved in every case by trying alternate captures/timestamps of the same or a byte-identical re-uploaded URL until one downloaded clean (verified: correct page count, zero pdfinfo syntax errors). ONE quarter could NOT be recovered this way: Q3 2018 (Third-Q-Statement-2018.pdf / Third-Q-Statement-2018-1.pdf) has FIVE independent Wayback captures across 2019-2024, all sharing the identical content digest, and all are genuinely corrupt (pdfinfo: 'Top-level pages object is wrong type (null)', zero recoverable pages) -- this appears to be a permanently corrupted file on the bank's own historical server, not a crawl-truncation artifact, since every independent crawl over 5 years captured the same broken bytes. No 2018_Q3.json was created; this is recorded as a genuine, permanent source gap, not a research shortfall. SEPARATE FINDING (not a parsing error, both sides internally consistent): each of these filings' own prior-year-end comparative Total Assets figure (e.g. Q1 2018's 31-Dec-2017 column) is consistently ~0.15-0.23% LOWER than this dataset's already-stored 2017/2018/2019_Q4.json total_assets figures. Likely explanation: the stored 2015-2019 Q4 figures in this dataset were sourced from a later annual report's multi-year 'Five-Year Summary' table (per this bank's own reporting_basis note above, which already documents a ~0.1-0.2% internal Assets-vs-Liabilities+Equity inconsistency within that same summary table), whereas these interim filings' comparative columns come directly from each year's own primary, contemporaneous Balance Sheet. This gap disappears entirely from FY2020 onward (2020_Q4.json onward was sourced from primary Balance Sheet/Annexure-B tables directly, per the reporting_basis note) -- confirmed by an exact, to-the-taka match between every 2021-2025 interim filing's comparative column and the corresponding already-stored Q4 figure. Per this project's 'record, don't reconcile' convention, this small pre-crisis discrepancy is noted here verbatim; the existing 2017/2018/2019_Q4.json files were NOT modified.
